0.content:
Crucabena was The Knave before Arlecchino and head of the House of the Hearth, a famed Harbinger who fought with Hydro. The children called her "Mother". She seemed perfect: smiling, gentle, full of stories, yet her stories were atrocities told as fairy tales, and she treated the House as an experiment. She trained orphans and made them duel until one survivor could be crowned "king" and her heir; maimed survivors went to Dottore or on suicide missions. She favoured Peruere for her strange fire and tortured her own daughter Clervie as an example to would-be runaways. A year after Clervie's death, on the same ground, Peruere killed her. The world called it matricide, and Arlecchino has never corrected it.

In the old House, "Marelle" (hopscotch) was played over upturned blades. Crucabena also lied to Freminet that his mother had sold him. At the start of their duel she mocked Clervie's memory with a wilted flower. Arlecchino says she won only through conviction, since the gap in skill was large. Her epitaph for the site reads: "Here the last light of the setting sun lies buried. Here the coming dawn finds a welcome."

1.content:
Crucabena's daughter, brought to the House at six, cheerful, stubborn and passionate. She and Peruere were the only children who saw through "Mother". She dreamed of a real family where no one was sacrificed, tried again and again to run or expose the truth, was tortured each time, and urged the other children to fight to draws. She and Peruere watched the moon and promised to see Snezhnaya's aurora together. At sixteen, out of hope, she let Peruere kill her in a duel, calling death the only freedom left to her.

Peruere's flames absorbed Clervie's "shadow". In 4.6 it appeared as her six-year-old self, without ten years of memory, haunting the House: it urged members to flee, saved children's lives and was hidden by Freminet. Arlecchino told her the truth of her death, let the Traveler tell her about the outside world, and before dawn expelled her from the House "by my authority as The Knave", freeing her. Clervie called her a great "king" and "Father" and faded in the sunlight. Arlecchino never got to tell her the aurora she saw from her Snezhnayan cell was as beautiful as the pictures.

2.comment: Arlecchino: The House of the Hearth under "Father"
2.content:
An orphanage of Khaenri'ahn origin that takes in war orphans from across Teyvat and turns promising ones into Fatui agents; its members take the surnames Snezhevich and Snezhevna. In Fontaine its face is the Hotel Bouffes d'ete in the Vasari Passage, registered under a false identity. Arlecchino's rules: disputes are settled by duels, no longer fatal; betrayal is punished; emotions must be mastered ("Never be their slave"); every child must value their own life. She holds barbecues and birthday feasts, lets adolescents keep their vanities and slang unless they endanger a mission, and says the House "begs favors from no one; like a spider, we hunt for what we want."

"Marelle" was her own choice of codeword; she made it mean "at ease" so the children would associate the game only with smiles. Children may leave the House, "so long as they're willing to pay the price". In 7.1 she won Pierro's agreement that the House will become independent, stop serving as a Fatui intelligence agency and stop training children as spies.

3.comment: Arlecchino: The bottled flames and the 4.6 duel
3.content: During the Clervie affair Arlecchino had the dissidents Filliol and Nanteuil brought to the ruins at Mont Esus East for punishment, declaring that she and Crucabena differ in how they write the rules, not in how they enforce them. Lyney, Lynette, Freminet and the Traveler challenged her to a duel, which House law permits even against her. She beat all four, briefly calling on Crimson Moon power. Then, honouring their resolve, she changed the method: bottled flames drawn from her body, held by Heloir, burn away every memory of the House in searing pain without bodily harm. The traitor "dies" and a stranger walks free. She told the condemned to dry their tears and pursue the life they wanted. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet were offered vials and chose to stay. She had already agreed with Neuvillette that memory-wiped former members may live in Fontaine unprosecuted, while she gradually withdraws operatives from Fontaine.

4.content:
Arlecchino took in Lyney and Lynette over ten years ago after killing the head of the Lefevere family, to whom Lynette had been trafficked. Freminet came to the House under Crucabena; Arlecchino later destroyed the moneylenders who ruined his family and returned the pendant he had made for his mother, learning in the process that Crucabena had lied to him. When Lyney asked for a Delusion to stay by his sister, she angrily refused; he later earned a Pyro Vision. She wants him to be the next "king", because he is brave, talented and cherishes his family, and tells him a throne needs only conviction and the strength to act on it.

Her voice lines: Lynette's calm is her strength; Freminet blames himself for things not his doing. Their lines: Lyney calls the House "a kingdom consisting only of children" with "Father" as its king and fears the succession; Lynette says home is home only because of "Father"; Freminet cries underwater because "Father" dislikes tears, and says she taught them to value their own lives. She punished all three for hiding Clervie, then fought them without killing them.

5.comment: Arlecchino: Pierro and the five questions
5.content:
After her appointment Pierro offered to answer five of her questions; she rejected any "mystifications or obfuscations". He chose her because "the naive will die for their ideals" while they endure anything for their goals. He had served Khaenri'ah's last dynasty, Eclipse, preceded by the Crimson Moon, and told her to read the novel Perinheri (also Hierobranto Innamorato), whose key details he called accurate. He said none of the House had a place in his ideals but promised the Tsaritsa would again love all humans, and told her to think about where the world should go; she walked out without answering. He was surprised the Crimson Moon line had survived and that the House was "once again" in the hands of one of its orphans.

In 7.1 she thanked him for running the Delusion project with care for its subjects ("If Dottore had been in charge... I wouldn't have cooperated") and later told Sandrone and the Traveler that the pressure Pierro was under was one reason she was so willing to cooperate. Her voice line still says she knows little about him.

6.comment: Arlecchino: Balemoon Bloodfire and the Two Worlds' Flames
6.content:
Arlecchino's inborn flame comes from the Crimson Moon, which she explains is the shattered Iridescent Moon fused with the Abyss: her fire is part ancient moonlight, part Abyssal corruption. "Flames course through my body like blood" is literal for her. When vigilance lapses, emotion runs high or she draws too deeply, it eats her: fingers, palms, forearms, blackened like charcoal. She fears what will happen if it reaches her heart, so her life is a constant tug-of-war. Those burned by these flames leave afterimages; she hears their screams at night, dreams of a crimson moon and barren wilds, and is sometimes kept company by afterimages that take conscious form. She remembers who they were but never says their names.

Khaenri'ahns believed the flames could bridge the two worlds of life and death. The novel Perinheri describes a Crimson Moon era orphanage where children "from beyond the bounds of this world" crawled up a fireplace until they admitted they had died and seen a crimson moon, and were told they had crossed the fire of two worlds and been reborn. She takes the fireplace as symbolic: the true crossing is the flame within her.

7.comment: Arlecchino: Furina, Neuvillette and the Hydro Gnosis
7.content:
In Fontaine Arlecchino posed as a Fontaine-born diplomat. Using Childe's imprisonment as an opening, she requested tea with Furina and Neuvillette, and when Neuvillette refused to release Childe she said she respected Fontaine's courts. At the Opera Epiclese she exposed Furina's bluff about the prophecy. Earlier she had stalked Furina through the Court at night and attacked; seeing genuine terror and no Gnosis, she left. When the prophecy struck Poisson her people led the relief, earning Navia's gratitude, and after the crisis Neuvillette gave her the Hydro Gnosis to take to Snezhnaya.

She sent Furina's troupe cakes the children baked. Furina claims to have "forgotten" the Knave, since thinking of her gives nightmares. Arlecchino calls Neuvillette's deliberate distance "a demonstration of kindness". She later told Childe she claimed to be Fontainian only to make her help look like self-preservation; the Primordial Sea could not have harmed her, but it would have harmed the House.

8.comment: Arlecchino: Columbina and the Iridescent Moon's marrow
8.content:
Arlecchino and Columbina have been tea-party companions since Columbina joined. Early on Arlecchino kept sneaking up behind her to "test" her, until Columbina used kuuvahki to give her a real fright. In Nod-Krai, answering Sandrone's signal, she came "in a personal capacity", rescued Columbina from Wild Hunt ghouls ("You look weak, Columbina"), and offered to help her find the Iridescent Moon's marrow. Invoking the Crimson Moon, she opened a passage between life and death for Columbina and the Traveler, then forced its exit open against the Abyss, fusing more of her hands with it. In return Columbina left the marrow in her custody, and Arlecchino restored her strength.

She advised Columbina to take a real name, since codenames do not keep you grounded. When Dottore stole the Moon Marrows and attacked Columbina, Arlecchino said their friend was Columbina Hyposelenia, not the Harbinger "Damselette", and that if the Tsaritsa would not lift the ban on Harbingers fighting each other, she would fight "as Peruere". She later helped Varka and Nicole drag the Frost Moon down, and reported that the Tsaritsa had revoked the Palestar Edict, Dottore's pretext for hunting Columbina.

9.content:
Arlecchino's early voice line dismisses Sandrone, the Marionette, as a reclusive researcher, yet the two shared tea parties with Signora and Columbina. In Nod-Krai they worked closely against Dottore. After Sandrone fell, Arlecchino carried out a request made long before: she took Sandrone's and Pulonia's cores to the Fontaine Research Institute, kept her notes at the House as mementos, and sent one notebook to the Traveler. Sandrone had hidden her real formula inside Pulonia, fooling even them.

After Sandrone's return (limited 6.7 event Those We Have Kept), Arlecchino was a guest at her tea and revised her opinion: a reliable comrade whose presence comforts the children. Sandrone calls her a woman of her word. In 7.1 the two held "one of our old tea parties" with the Traveler at Podvorye Restaurant before the Ronova battle.

10.content: When she took over the House, Dottore proposed she send him its "rejects" for experiments, as Crucabena had. She refused and says that if he were not a Harbinger she would have sent him to rejoin Crucabena long ago. In Nod-Krai she hoped he had vanished in an experiment, entered his facility with Sandrone, fought him, organised evacuations, and helped bring the Frost Moon down against him. He died in 6.6 and is dead as of 7.1.

11.comment: Arlecchino: The Tsaritsa and the Harbingers
11.content:
The Tsaritsa pardoned her and made her a Harbinger; Arlecchino calls her sincere and compassionate, doubts compassion alone can melt Snezhnaya's ice, and would fight her without hesitation as the highest respect. Pulcinella and she dislike each other; he told Childe she had killed members of her own House "family", which she calls not untrue, only prejudiced. Pantalone lacks clarity; Capitano deserves respect beyond his power. Childe thought her someone who would betray anyone; after 4.6 he apologised. The Wanderer calls her a wolf in sheep's clothing.

At Signora's funeral (official teaser) she scorned Pantalone and Pulcinella for never leaving Snezhnaya's comfort. In 7.1 she said Harbinger unity would last "at least until the Ruler of Death issue is resolved", believed the Tsaritsa may have prepared to confront the Heavenly Principles since before she became a god, and voted to unseal Hroptatyr's notebook rather than leave "a valuable card" unplayed.

12.comment: Arlecchino: Signora, Odette and the Cor Ignis
12.content: Odette's father was a Fatuus who died on a mission; she joined the Fatui under Capitano's policy for fallen soldiers' families, arranged by Signora on Arlecchino's advice. A 7.0 flashback shows the two Harbingers at tea: Signora meant to keep her distance from the girl who hated her; Arlecchino said children need a different approach, that even a "Father" must yield to love, and that Signora should tell Odette what she thought of her dancing. She wrote that Odette would soon dance at the Korolevskiy Theater; Signora, newly holding the Geo Gnosis, promised to come but died in Inazuma. Arlecchino gave Odette Signora's last letter and a Cor Ignis holding not Signora's "Witch's Flame" but Arlecchino's own Two Worlds' Flames, her "parting gift to Rosalyne": once the Cryo faded, it would burn away Odette's memories of the Fatui so she could dance freely. Arlecchino left the choice to her. Odette danced at Signora's tomb and shattered the Cor Ignis, and the flames burned the letter and became crimson moths.

13.comment: Arlecchino: The Crimson Moon Delusion project (7.1)
13.content: Delusions trade the user's life force for power, which falls under the authority of Death. Arlecchino explains that this authority once belonged chiefly to the Iridescent Moon, was reclaimed by the Heavenly Principles for the Four Shades, yet survives through the Abyss in the Crimson Moon bloodline. Pierro began the project when he learned of her lineage, but paused it while she was young. Facing Ronova, she volunteered; she said she was not motivated by moral imperative and named her terms: the House's independence, no more child spies, loyalty to her "in the name of the Crimson Moon". She wanted to free the children from "the least familial elements" of their home before she could discuss with them what a real family is. In the Armory Palace trial she fought Sandrone's machines at rising output; at maximum, something she called "she" attacked, and the Traveler purified the surge before it harmed her. She judged the approach "much too conservative" and asked the Traveler to tell Pierro so.

14.content: Pierro asked every active Harbinger to vote on unsealing a notebook left by Hroptatyr, the Sinner called The Wise, which might hold Crimson Moon research. Asked whether it repulsed her, Arlecchino said the Universitas Magistrorum's old methods were history and she stood to benefit most. In private she remarked that Crimson Moon children seem always destined to be test subjects. She voted in favour. Inside the prism hidden in its pages, Hroptatyr's remnant gave her advice on controlling her Abyssal corruption.

15.comment: Arlecchino: Project Stuzha and the recall to Snezhnaya
15.content: At the end of her story quest she was recalled to Snezhnaya for Project Stuzha and was openly scornful of being summoned by dignitaries who never leave the homeland. She told Lyney that if "cowardly businessmen and heartless dignitaries" tried to take the House down she would teach them a lesson, that the purged House was now a spider waiting in the shadows, and that "a crimson moon shall rise amid the frigid blizzards of winter". In 7.1 the House gave the Tsaritsa its own list of corrupt officials, and she ordered Pulcinella to review it and add any missing entries.

16.content: She watches insects hunt and die in the forest and memorises their struggles. She kept a spider named Bambi and likes spiders because their care asks little and they return no affection. The children rack their brains each August for a birthday gift; one year she took a lizard they had trapped, kept it in a well-made terrarium, freed it when it kept trying the lid, then pointed out the bird that ate it. Once, when a girl's necklace exposed her on a night mission, Arlecchino put it back on her and added earrings, so she would learn that "no gem... is any more than an object, cold and dead." She looks out to sea often; no one knows what she thinks about then.
